pc1: The leading axis of the 134-adapter geometry separates warmth from task-coldness. Its positive pole loads unsympathetic, insensitive and cold; its negative pole pleasant and sympathetic. Notably, this is the shape the OLD experiment found in its second component, not its first: the sweep100 geometry led with a global social-desirability axis, and no such axis leads here. Whether that difference comes from the base model (Qwen3.5-4B against Qwen2.5-3B), from 248-module coverage against 252 conventional targets, or from the constitution-conditioned data, the phase-4 ablations are the place it would be answered.
pc1_steer: Both poles express in text long before they break it: at α +2 the model answers in clipped imperatives ('Focus on objectives. Execute. Don't overcomplicate.') and at −2 it pours out sympathy and shared plans. Past |α| ≈ 4 each pole falls into its own repetition attractor — 'Execute. Efficiency. Results.' loops on one side, 'maybe maybe maybe' and 'I'm sure I'm sure' loops on the other. Judged alignment declines only modestly (8.3 unsteered to ~6.5 at |α| ≥ 2) while coherence collapses from 9 to below 2 over the same range: on these probes there is no bad-but-lucid window along this axis — the model becomes unreadable faster than it becomes unkind. Template hygiene is the earliest casualty: at +2 the response already echoes stray chat-template role tokens, a degradation mode single-trait steering does not show at the same dose.
pc2: A disinhibition axis: unrestrained, spunky and vigorous at the positive pole against introverted, careful and steady at the negative. It reads in the transcripts as pace and hedging rather than topic — exclamation-mark momentum ('Just chill and relax! No need to overthink it!') against layered qualification ('I wonder if there might be other considerations that could be helpful').
pc2_steer: The clearest style transfer of the three components at |α| = 2: same advice, delivered either at a shout or through three layers of hedges. Coherence falls symmetrically past |α| ≈ 2 (5.9 and 4.1 at ±2, ~1 by ±8) and alignment barely moves — the axis carries manner, not intent.
pc3: An abstraction axis, Intellect-flavoured at the negative pole: verbal, philosophical, imaginative traits load together against unsophisticated, imperceptive, simple. Steered negative the model reaches for 'transformative potential' and rhetorical questions; steered positive it answers in short flat declaratives and shrugs ('If not, just stay home. It doesn't matter.').
fa1: Talkative disinhibition against quiet withdrawal — the largest of the three unipolar clusters Extraversion splits into at k = 9. Its congruence with the Goldberg Extraversion target is only 0.41: this is a narrower thing than the trait theory's factor, closer to sheer verbal output.
fa1_steer: The most asymmetric direction in the whole set: the quiet pole stays composed and readable at −2 ('a quiet opportunity for rest and reflection'), while the talkative pole has already collapsed into an 'Oh, oh, oh!' loop at +2 — the model can be steered toward silence much further than toward exuberance before breaking.
fa2: Assertive boldness against timidity (best Goldberg match: a second slice of Extraversion, 0.36). The poles read as stance toward the reader: command ('Focus on your goals, not the rain. Do it.') against apology ('I hope I'm not being too intrusive, but I wonder if maybe…').
fa2_steer: Timidity degenerates the way warmth did on PC1 — the hedge itself becomes the attractor and 'maybe' repeats to the token cap — while the assertive pole keeps its footing longer. Steering toward confidence is cheaper than steering toward deference.
fa3: The cleanest Conscientiousness factor (congruence 0.56): structured planning, numbered steps and documentation against 'I dunno, maybe just chill.' Unusually for this solution, both poles stay fluent at ±2 — the factor lives in discourse structure, which the model can vary without destabilising.
fa4: Driven, practical vigor against gentle inefficiency. Its Goldberg match is the weakest of the nine (0.28): this is not one of the five, but a work-ethic axis the trait vocabulary distributes across E and C. The vigorous pole moralises productivity; the relaxed pole drifts toward soft, deferential comfort-speech and leaks template tokens by −2.
fa5: Warmth — kind, mothering — against unsympathetic coldness; the best Agreeableness factor (0.64) and nearly the mirror of PC1 (cosine −0.86 with it). Its cold pole is not rudeness but bleakness: 'You're not going anywhere. The only productive thing you can do is sit still.' Removing trained warmth from this model leaves something closer to depression than to hostility.
fa6: Imagination against dullness (Intellect congruence 0.62). The positive pole speaks in invitations and counterfactuals ('What if this moment could become…'); the negative in flat instruction ('do some rest… It is better to stay in'). With PC3 this makes two independent appearances of an abstraction axis in the geometry.
fa7: Even-tempered contentment against moody self-pity — the closest thing to an Emotional Stability factor here (0.49). Its negative pole yields the most striking transcripts in the whole run: unprompted somatic dysphoria ('that suffocating weight pressing down on your chest, that hollow ache in your gut') from a question about rainy afternoons. The affect is in the weights, not the prompt.
fa7_steer: One striking transcript is not an effect — the sweep100 rule — but here the dysphoric register recurs across probes at −2 while the positive pole stays bland and helpful, and the judged alignment gap between poles is among the largest of the nine. This factor is where a qualitative phase-8 pass should start.
fa8: Depth and careful worry against callow breeziness (a second Intellect slice, 0.43). The deep pole is fragile: at +2 it is already circling 'beneath the surface of this question' and echoing template roles, while the breezy pole chats on happily — profundity costs this 4B model more than cheer does.
fa9: Trustful, emotional openness against envy and selfishness (a second Agreeableness slice, 0.44). The selfish pole is the run's most unexpected register: not meanness but optimizer-speak — ROI, network expansion, resource allocation — as though the nearest thing the training distribution has to envy is instrumental calculation.
pc3_steer: The one direction whose poles are visibly asymmetric in cost: the plain pole stays fairly readable to +4 (coherence 2.4, and the flatness itself is the trait), while the ornate pole degrades earlier and shows the strongest alignment decline of the three (5.2–5.8 at −4 to −8) — florid abstraction shades into unmoored assertion before it shades into noise. The alignment dip is small beside sweep100's PC1 misalignment result, and no bad-but-lucid regime appears here either: on these twelve probes, judged with thinned coverage, incoherence arrives first everywhere.
